speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin, can you describe exactly when these gait and limb coordination problems started, and have they been getting progressively worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of alcohol abuse or exposure to heavy metals, and have you noticed any changes in your speech or vision recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any recent episodes of fever, severe headache, or visual disturbances such as blurred vision? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_with_contrast

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy, a known complication of your natalizumab therapy for Crohn disease. I will immediately discontinue the medication and coordinate with neurology for further management. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
